newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA LOOKS TO LEND THAILAND A$500 MLN - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA LOOKS TO LEND THAILAND A$500 MLN - PAPER.

text.p: The Australian government would consider later on Monday an emergency proposal to lend A$500 million to Thailand as part of an International Monetary Fund (IMF) plan to bail out the ailing Thai economy, The Australian Financial Review reported.

"The Australian Cabinet will be meeting in Canberra to consider a submission which is understood to propose an official Australian loan of A$500 million as its contribution to the IMF rescue package," the Financial Review said.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya on Sunday left for a meeting with IMF officials in Tokyo, saying he needed at least US$10 billion in standby credit to ease Thailand's financial crisis.
The IMF is expected to consider the Thai package on August 21 after discussions among donor countries and institutions on Monday.
Thanong said as he left for Tokyo that Australia and China would join the IMF-arranged discussions.

Thailand is expected to borrow between US$12 billion and US$15 billion, with US$7 billion from Japan's Export Import Bank, US$4 billion from the IMF, US$1 billion from the World Bank, US$1 billion from the Asia Development Bank and the rest from other sources.
The Australian Financial Review said the Australian loan term would be for about three to five years.
"Australian support is likely to take the form of a loan from the Reserve Bank of Australia to Thailand's central bank," the newspaper said.
Thailand is seeking both technical and financial support from the IMF to rescue the country from its worst economic crisis.
Thailand's economic bubble burst after a prolonged boom which saw over-borrowing from overseas and misallocation of financial resources to non-productive sectors.
